about.title: Berkeley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Berkeley packs a lot of movement into a small footprint. In 2025, the city recorded 603 injury collisions, with 775 people hurt and 6 lives lost, according to public collision records. Those counts run highest along I-80, University Avenue, Ashby Avenue, and Shattuck, and they climb on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters, students, and delivery traffic all share the same lanes. If one of those crashes was yours, the days that follow can feel oddly quiet and overwhelming at the same time: a rental car to arrange, a doctor to see, an adjuster calling before you have caught your breath. LawProactive exists to make one part simpler. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches Berkeley residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Alameda County car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing to be connected, and the attorney only earns a fee if your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Berkeley Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines that differ by defendant
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but a claim involving a city bus, a public vehicle, or a road maintained by a government agency can require a formal claim in as little as six months. An attorney can sort out which clock applies to your Berkeley crash before it runs out.

items.title: Shared fault does not end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible; your share of the blame simply reduces the amount. Insurers know this, which is why they push hard for a recorded statement early on, and why it is wise to decline one until you have spoken with an attorney.

items.title: No cap on what your suffering is worth
items.desc: California places no ceiling on non-economic damages in a car accident case, so pain, lost sleep, and the disruption to your daily life all count. Preserving photos, dashcam footage, witness contacts, and medical records helps an attorney document that full picture.

items.question: I was hit on I-80 near the Berkeley exits but the other driver's insurer says I was partly at fault. Do I still have a case?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning a percentage of blame reduces your recovery rather than eliminating it. Even if the insurer assigns you some fault for a merge or lane change, you can still pursue compensation for the remaining share. An independent attorney can review the police report and evidence to challenge how that percentage was assigned.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and most attorneys recommend that you politely decline until you have counsel. Adjusters often ask questions designed to lock in details you may not remember accurately in the days after a crash. You can still report the accident to your own insurer as your policy requires.

items.question: How long do I have to act after a Berkeley car accident?
items.answer: For most claims against another private driver, California allows two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, such as a city-owned vehicle or a roadway design issue, a written claim may need to be filed within six months. Because that shorter window passes quickly, it helps to have an attorney evaluate your situation soon after the collision.
